Understanding Substance Abuse

Understanding Substance Abuse

Substance abuse involves the harmful or hazardous use of psychoactive substances, including alcohol and illicit drugs. It can lead to addiction, a chronic, relapsing disorder characterized by compulsive drug seeking and use despite harmful consequences.

Cravings — Intense urges to use the substance

Loss of Control — Inability to limit or stop substance use

Withdrawal Symptoms — Physical and mental symptoms when stopping or reducing use

Neglect of Responsibilities — Ignoring obligations at work, school, or home

Continued Use Despite Harm — Persisting despite knowing the adverse effects on health

28%

Quit Rate with TMS

Clinical Results

Evidence and Outcomes for Smoking Cessation

BrainsWay® Deep TMS using the H4 Coil targets brain networks involved in addiction and has demonstrated meaningful clinical outcomes in controlled research.

In a prospective, double-blind, multicenter study of adults with long-term smoking histories and multiple previous quit attempts, those who completed active Deep TMS treatment showed a continuous quit rate of about 28%, compared with approximately 11.7% in the sham control group, based on four consecutive weeks of abstinence confirmed by self-report and urine testing.

Comprehensive Care

Integrative, Full-Spectrum Support

Deep TMS for substance use is offered as part of a comprehensive treatment plan that can include:

Medication Management

Addressing withdrawal, co-occurring conditions, or relapse triggers with evidence-based pharmacotherapy.

Targeted Lab Testing

Assessing medical contributors such as metabolic and stress biomarkers to inform treatment.

Evidence-Based Supplements

Supporting neurochemical balance when appropriate under physician guidance, never as a replacement for medical treatment.

Behavioral & Psychosocial Support

Bolstering motivation and coping skills to support lasting change and recovery.

TMS is not a stand-alone "magic cure," but when integrated with personalized care under physician direction, it can be a valuable component of a supportive strategy for those ready to make a change.

The Science

How TMS Works for Substance Abuse

Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) targets specific areas of the brain involved in addiction and impulse control. By delivering magnetic pulses to these regions, TMS can help modulate neural activity, reducing cravings and improving self-control. This can make it easier to resist the urge to use substances and support long-term recovery.

Reduction in Cravings

Many patients experience a significant decrease in cravings, making it easier to abstain from substance use.

Non-Invasive & Drug-Free

TMS is a non-invasive procedure that does not require medication, avoiding potential side effects of pharmaceuticals.

Long-Term Recovery Support

By improving brain function and reducing cravings, TMS enhances the effectiveness of other addiction treatments and supports long-term recovery.

Your Journey

The TMS Treatment Process

01

Comprehensive Evaluation

Your journey begins with a comprehensive evaluation. Our team assesses your medical history, current symptoms, and treatment goals to determine if TMS is the right choice for you.

02

Personalized TMS Sessions

TMS sessions typically last about 20-40 minutes and are conducted five days a week for several weeks. You'll sit comfortably while the device delivers magnetic pulses—no anesthesia needed, resume normal activities immediately.

03

Continuous Support

Our team provides continuous support throughout the treatment process, closely monitoring your progress and making necessary adjustments to ensure optimal results and help you regain control of your life.
